doc: Design matter: change a material's row or a law and see the same scene under the new definition, try a change before making it, keep every step as a commit, and hold the part you are working on.

tools.name: lab.describe
tools.description: What is being designed: each source with its lines and hash — a material a file (materials/wood.json), the laws (laws.json), the look (look.json), the scene (scene.json) — the world's shape and steps, the commit shown, whether there are changes not committed, and the claims held

budget.description: the most bytes of answer: the sources are then counted, not listed

tools.name: lab.read
tools.description: One source's text as it is now

path.description: as lab.describe lists it: materials/<name>.json, laws.json, look.json, scene.json

tools.name: lab.edit
tools.description: One source's text replaced, made or removed: the definition is prepared, the look checked and the scene played again under them, to the same step, before anything is replaced — a text with a problem changes nothing and says where. Answers what changed in the world (cells that differ, materials then and now) and its commit
tools.undo: lab.revert to the commit before it (`HEAD~1`)

text.description: its whole text, JSON (kept a row a line)

remove.description: a boolean (its id): the source taken away (a material's row)

intent.description: what the change is for: its commit's message

tools.name: lab.material
tools.description: One material's row: made when it is not there, properties set (null takes one away) or the row removed — its own source changed and nothing else, the scene played again. Answers as lab.edit
tools.undo: lab.revert to the commit before it (`HEAD~1`)

properties.description: {property: value} — numbers, a phase's name, another material's name, tags as a list; null removes one

remove.description: a boolean (its id): the row taken away (refused while a material or the scene names it)

intent.description: what the change is for: its commit's message

tools.name: lab.law
tools.description: One law by its name: replaced where it stands, added after the last when it is new, or removed. A law reads properties and never a material's name (refused otherwise). Answers as lab.edit
tools.undo: lab.revert to the commit before it (`HEAD~1`)

law.description: the law without its name: {when, add | take | set | raise | become, event?, flag?} or {transfer, by | shift}

remove.description: a boolean (its id): the law taken away

intent.description: what the change is for: its commit's message

tools.name: lab.try
tools.description: What a change would do, nothing changed: the same scene played under the changed sources and under these, some steps on — cells that differ, materials in each, what happened in each counted by name

material.description: a material whose row is changed, with `properties` as lab.material takes them

path.description: or a source's path, with `text` as lab.edit takes it

steps.description: steps run on after the scene's own, in both (0 when none is given)

tools.name: lab.reset
tools.description: The scene begun anew: a field of a shape filled with one material, nothing placed, no step run. Answers as lab.edit
tools.undo: lab.revert to the commit before it (`HEAD~1`)

shape.description: [width, height] in cells (as it is when none is given)

filled.description: the material every cell is (as it is when none is given)

intent.description: what the change is for: its commit's message

tools.name: lab.explain
tools.description: Why a part of the design is what it is: the commits that changed its source, newest first — who, what for, the lines before and after — and who holds it now. With a property: the line that says it and the commit that last wrote that line

property.description: a property of a material's row, or any member's key in the source

limit.description: the most commits answered (10 when none is given)

tools.name: lab.picture
tools.description: The field as it looks now — every cell by the look, its light as a glow — as a PNG kept beside the lab by its content: its path, size and hash

scale.description: pixels a cell (the lab's own when none is given; 1 … 16)

tools.name: lab.history
tools.description: The design's history: the branch worked on, branches and tags, a branch's commits newest first — each with who made it — and whether what runs has changes not committed

branch.description: this branch's commits (the one worked on when none is given)

limit.description: the most commits (50 when none is given)

tools.name: lab.commit
tools.description: What runs now kept as a commit on the branch worked on, with its picture (a change of the definition keeps itself; this keeps what was placed in the scene since)
tools.undo: lab.revert to the commit before it (`HEAD~1`)

tools.name: lab.branch
tools.description: A branch made at a commit (the one worked on when none is given); work stays where it is
tools.undo: a branch is left behind by switching away; nothing is lost

at.description: a branch, a tag or a commit

tools.name: lab.switch
tools.description: Another branch's, tag's or commit's sources put into what runs: its definition prepared, its scene played; refused while there are changes not committed, unless forced

to.description: a branch, a tag or a commit

force.description: a boolean (its id): drop what is not committed

tools.name: lab.revert
tools.description: A commit's sources put back as a new commit: nothing of the history is lost
tools.undo: lab.revert to the commit before it (`HEAD~1`)

to.description: a branch, a tag or a commit (`HEAD~1`: the one before the last)

tools.name: lab.diff
tools.description: Where two states differ, by source and line: a commit against another, or against what runs now

from.description: a branch, a tag or a commit (the last commit when none is given)

to.description: another; what runs now when none is given

tools.name: lab.merge
tools.description: Another branch's changes brought into this one, by source and by line: two materials added on two branches are both there, two properties of one material both set; the same line changed on both merges nothing and says which sources. The merged definition is prepared and played before it is kept
tools.undo: lab.revert to the commit before it (`HEAD~1`)

from.description: a branch, a tag or a commit

tools.name: lab.tag
tools.description: A name given to a commit (the one worked on when none is given)
tools.undo: a tag stays; give another name

at.description: a branch, a tag or a commit

tools.name: lab.claim
tools.description: A part held while working on it: others' changes to it wait and are told who holds it and what for (a person is never held). A lease: asked again, it is renewed

part.description: materials/<name>, laws/<name>, look, scene — or `materials`, `laws` with `subtree` for all of them

subtree.description: a boolean (its id): the part and everything inside it

seconds.description: how long (30 when none is given; 1 … 600)

tools.name: lab.release
tools.description: A part let go (a person lets go of anyone's)

tools.name: lab.claims
tools.description: The parts held now: who, what for, how long yet

tasks.name: read-the-definition
tasks.summary: Read what the definition is made of, then one material's row

tasks.name: try-before-changing
tasks.summary: See the same scene under a changed row, beside the scene as it is, nothing changed

tasks.name: change-a-material-and-ask-why
tasks.summary: Change a property of a material, see the commit it made, and ask who set the property and why

tasks.name: take-a-change-back
tasks.summary: Make a change, compare it with the commit before, and go back to that commit

tasks.name: hold-the-part-you-work-on
tasks.summary: Say which part you are working on so others do not write over it, and let it go
